chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who passes by water in which there is a dead animal that has become putrid. He said: If the foul odor is predominant over the water, then he should not perform wudu (ablution) from it, nor drink from it.

key_terms.النَّتْنُ: the foul odor resulting from decay
key_terms.الْمَاءِ: water, the substance whose condition and usability are being judged
key_terms.دَابَّةٌ: a creature or animal found dead in the water
key_terms.مَيِّتَةٌ: dead carcass, indicating the source of contamination

ai.seo_question: Can water be used for wudu (ablution) or drinking if a dead animal has made its smell foul?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning water affected by a dead animal. If the stench of decay has overtaken the water, it is not to be used for wudu (ablution) and it is not to be drunk, indicating that perceptible change in the water's properties affects its ritual and practical usability.
